messages:
Sam K: FYI bringing up argo-embed-v1 with int4 per-channel quant for the whole vector. quick smoke looks like short-query recall tanked on product search test. need eyes.
Priya N: how big is the delta? short queries = single-token titles?
Sam K: yes, titles. baseline float32 recall@1=0.61, int4=0.45; recall@10 0.89 -> 0.73. longer-query and descriptions mostly fine.
Miguel R: that's a classic high-frequency-information loss in low-bit quant. did you apply whitening/mean-subtract before quant?
Sam K: pipeline: tokenize -> embed -> l2norm -> PCA(512) -> mean_subtract -> quantize(int4) -> store. noticing we do mean_subtract after PCA in offline index build but runtime does mean_subtract before PCA (old codepath).
Zoe P: mismatch there would shift centroids a lot. are you saying build-time and runtime order differ? :grimacing:
Sam K: yep. build-time: PCA then center; runtime: center then PCA. floats masked the difference but int4 amplified it.
Nora H: can we reproduce by taking a sample, run both orderings in float32 and compare nearest neighbors? should be deterministic.
Priya N: also check per-dimension zero-point clipping in the quantizer. int4 symmetric might be zero-centered but PCA loadings skewed positive/negative, so asymmetric quant + zero-point might help.
Sam K: running quick repro now. command: `tools/emb-harness.py --model argo-embed-v1 --sample 2000 --repro-ordering`
embed-ci-bot: started job argo-int4-repro/1751234567 - will post summary when done.
Miguel R: while that's running, thought: short queries rely on top principal components (few dims) more. did you inspect explained variance by PC pre/post quant?
Sam K: pulled numbers: float explained variance (PC1..3) = [0.22,0.11,0.07]; int4 quantized recon explained variance = [0.15,0.09,0.06]. so PC1 lost ~30% power.
Zoe P: that matches recall drop. try PCA components 768->512 change? also maybe we should keep PCA in float32 and only quantize final vector post-whitening.
Priya N: agree. simpler patch: enforce identical preprocessing ordering in both build/runtime and keep PCA weights as float32 (not fused into quant kernel).
Sam K: repro results: ordering mismatch replicates recall drop in float32 but much smaller. int4 reproduces full drop. attaching logs: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/reports/argo-int4/1751234567.
embed-ci-bot: report uploaded: includes recall curves, per-pc variance table, knn confusion, UMAP images.
Nora H: filing ticket ENG-MODEL-4890: PCA/centering ordering mismatch + suggested mitigation. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-platform.
Miguel R: for immediate mitigation, propose: 1) revert to int8 for short-query-critical index until we have ordering fixed; 2) add a small calibration step that learns a per-dim bias after quant to align PC means (cheap).
Zoe P: I'll add a note on the model card that argo-embed-v1-int4 is experimental and not for title-search workloads. also add CI test that runs a 1k short-query recall smoke to catch regressions.
Priya N: add unit test: assert PC1 explained variance ratio within 0.05 of baseline after quant pipeline; and assert mean L2 between build/runtime < 0.04.
Sam K: plan of record: patch runtime to match build ordering, re-run full holdout (50k) with int4/int8, land PCA float32 whitelist; keep int8 for production index until A/B passes.
embed-ci-bot: scheduled holdout run: argo-holdout/50k queued. ETA ~2h.
Sam K: thanks team. leaving thread open; will post final holdout numbers and PR link.
Zoe P: thanks Sam ":thumbsup:"
Miguel R: nice catch, good call on unit tests."
